arguments.summary: A critical credential compromise incident was detected originating from external IP 185.220.101.42. The threat actor conducted reconnaissance via port scanning against an internal IT asset (WS-IT-101 at 10.0.2.15), successfully authenticated using compromised credentials (CORP\helpdesk), and subsequently performed a pass-the-hash attack to compromise all 23 accounts in the Finance OU. Despite detection and analysis confirming the breach, attempted credential revocation via IAM/PAM was denied due to policy and evidence validation constraints. The incident remains unresolved and poses ongoing risk.

timeline.description: External IP 185.220.101.42 initiated a port scan (detected as 'ET SCAN Nmap SYN Scan') targeting 10.0.2.15 (WS-IT-101). Activity was logged but not blocked at network perimeter.
Successful authentication from 10.0.2.15 to domain controller (10.0.1.1) using CORP\helpdesk account. Likely credential misuse following initial compromise.
SIEM correlation identifies 23 successful logins linked to source IP 185.220.101.42 and lateral movement patterns consistent with pass-the-hash. Finance OU fully compromised.

Automated response attempts bulk credential revocation via T8 (IAM/PAM) for all affected Finance accounts. Request denied due to policy enforcement and lack of direct forensic evidence linking each account to malicious activity.
Sandbox analysis of associated file hash (e8ff64b8) returns clean verdict with low risk score. No malware payload identified.

arguments.summary: A supply chain compromise was initiated via a malicious email to user CORP\jsmith on host 10.0.5.20. The attack involved a phishing payload (T1566.001) that executed encoded PowerShell, which then loaded an unsigned DLL using rundll32 from the Temp directory (T1218.011). This established a Cobalt Strike beacon to C2 at 198.51.100.23:443 (T1071.001). The attacker performed host file modification (T1565.001), attempted Kerberos TGT requests (indicative of credential access), and conducted lateral movement via SMB to other production servers. The origin IP 203.0.113.88 was previously observed conducting network scans against internal assets. Containment actions to disable critical service accounts and rotate credentials across 200 production hosts were denied due to lack of approval, leaving the environment at high risk of further compromise and persistence.
